baseline_comparison.strategy: Drive to the farthest reachable station, fill the tank, repeat (prices ignored).

assumptions: The vehicle starts with a full 50-gallon tank (500 miles at 10 mpg). That fuel was not bought at a listed station, so it is valued at the average price of stations near the route (initial_tank_reference_price_per_gallon).

Each stop buys only the fuel needed to reach a cheaper stop or the destination, or fills the tank when no cheaper stop is in range. amount_paid_at_stops_usd is cash spent at the pumps; total_fuel_cost_usd is the value of the fuel actually burned.
The CSV has no coordinates. Each station is placed at its city's ZIP-code centroid, so route_mile and off-route distances are approximate.
Visiting a station adds a round trip of twice its straight-line distance from the route. That extra driving burns fuel and counts against the range.
A station listed on several CSV rows is priced at the mean of those rows. Canadian rows and prices outside $1-$10 are ignored.
Prices come from the supplied CSV, not live data. Routes come from OpenRouteService (driving-car profile).
